lead: Electronic fuel injection (EFI) replaces the carburettor with a control loop. Sensors measure air flow, throttle angle, coolant temperature, exhaust oxygen and crank position. An electronic control unit (ECU) turns these signals into an injector pulse width. A fuel pump and pressure regulator keep fuel pressure fixed, so pulse width sets the fuel mass. EFI is used on almost every new petrol car, motorcycle and scooter in India because it holds the air-fuel ratio close to stoichiometric and cuts emissions.
prereq: You need: Chapter 2.2 for injection requirements and types, and Chapter 2.4 for the high-pressure rail idea behind direct injection.

blocks.text: The loop has five parts. Sensors turn physical quantities into voltages. The ECU is a microprocessor with lookup tables and correction maps. Injectors are solenoid valves (some newer ones are piezo) that open when current flows. The fuel pump supplies more fuel than the engine needs. The pressure regulator returns the excess to the tank and holds delivery pressure constant, commonly about 3 bar for port injection. Because pressure is fixed, the ECU meters fuel only by changing injector open time, called pulse width.

items: Air flow sensor: hot-wire or hot-film type measures intake air mass; a manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor is used instead on speed-density systems.
Throttle position sensor (TPS): a potentiometer or Hall sensor reports idle, part load and wide-open throttle.
Coolant temperature sensor: a thermistor enriches the mixture when the engine is cold.
Crank position sensor: a magnetic or Hall pickup on the flywheel gives engine speed and piston position, so the ECU knows when to inject.
Oxygen sensor: a zirconia cell in the exhaust gives a voltage that switches either side of stoichiometric, about 14.7:1 by mass for petrol.

blocks.text: Open loop means the ECU uses tables only, with no oxygen feedback. It runs open loop during cold start, hard acceleration and wide-open throttle. Closed loop means the oxygen sensor trims the pulse width to hold the mixture near stoichiometric. The trim has a short-term correction and a long-term learned correction.

sections.h3: Mono-point: one injector at the throttle body

blocks.text: Mono-point EFI uses one injector mounted above the throttle plate in a throttle body. The injector sprays fuel into the incoming air, and the mixture travels through the intake manifold to all cylinders. Some syllabi call this single-point or throttle-body injection (TBI).

Fuel pressure is low, about 1 bar above manifold pressure, and the injector fires at a fixed frequency, often once per engine revolution or twice per cycle. The ECU still uses the same sensors and oxygen feedback. Because fuel is delivered at one central point, cylinder-to-cylinder distribution depends on manifold geometry, so the mixture can be uneven. Wall wetting on a cold manifold also delays fuel response. Mono-point was a cheap retrofit for carburettors in the 1980s and 1990s. It is rare on new cars; multi-point and direct injection have replaced it.

Multi-point EFI (MPFI) has one injector per cylinder, mounted in the intake port just upstream of the inlet valve. Each injector sprays onto the back of the valve, so the fuel stays in the port and enters the cylinder as the valve opens. Port injection is another name. Fuel pressure is usually 3 to 4 bar.

Firing can be simultaneous, batch or sequential. In simultaneous firing all injectors open together once per revolution. In batch firing injectors are grouped, for example two groups that alternate. In sequential firing each injector opens just before its own cylinder's intake stroke. Sequential gives the best fuel control and cold-start behaviour but needs a cam or crank sensor that identifies the cylinder.

Compared with mono-point, MPFI gives better distribution, faster response and lower wall wetting. The intake manifold carries only air, so it can be tuned for air flow. The ECU can also cut fuel to one injector for a misfire or over-speed limit. MPFI is the common layout on Indian petrol cars and motorcycles.

Gasoline direct injection (GDI) puts the injector inside the combustion chamber, so fuel is sprayed directly into the cylinder. The fuel system runs at high pressure, typically 50 to 200 bar, because the injector must overcome cylinder pressure and still atomise. A high-pressure pump is driven by the camshaft; a common rail feeds the injectors, similar in idea to CRDI for diesel.

GDI can run homogeneous or stratified. In homogeneous charge the fuel is injected early in the intake stroke and mixed with all the air, giving a uniform mixture like port injection. In stratified charge the fuel is injected late in the compression stroke, so a rich cloud sits near the spark plug and the rest of the cylinder stays lean. Stratified operation saves fuel at part load but needs precise spray and timing.

Direct injection avoids fuel wetting the port walls and allows a higher compression ratio because the charge is cooled by evaporation. It also has problems: carbon deposits on intake valves, particulate matter, and more complex high-pressure hardware. GDI is not the same as port injection: the injector location and pressure are different.

examples.question: A port injector flows 240 cm³/min when fully open. The ECU holds it open for 5 ms. Find the fuel volume delivered in one injection in cm³ and mm³.
steps: Convert open time: 5 ms = 5 × 10⁻³ s = 0.005 s.
Volume = flow × time = 4 cm³/s × 0.005 s = 0.02 cm³.
Convert: 1 cm³ = 1000 mm³, so 0.02 cm³ = 20 mm³.
examples.answer: Fuel delivered per injection is 0.02 cm³, which is 20 mm³.
examples.check:
flow_cm3_per_min = 240
open_ms = 5
flow_cm3_per_s = flow_cm3_per_min / 60
open_s = open_ms / 1000
volume_cm3 = flow_cm3_per_s * open_s
volume_mm3 = volume_cm3 * 1000
print(volume_cm3)
print(volume_mm3)

traps: Mono-point does not mean one injector per cylinder. It means one injector in total, at the throttle body; multi-point has one per cylinder at the ports.
GDI is direct injection into the cylinder at high pressure, not port injection. Port pressure is about 3 bar; GDI pressure is tens to hundreds of bar.
Pulse width sets fuel mass only because pressure is held constant. If the pressure regulator fails, the same pulse width gives a different fuel mass.
Closed loop needs a hot oxygen sensor. A cold engine runs open loop, so the ECU ignores the oxygen signal during warm-up.
Sequential injection needs cylinder identification, not just crank speed. Batch and simultaneous firing can run from a crank sensor alone.

quiz.q: What does the ECU change to meter fuel in a port injection system?
quiz.a: Pulse width, the injector open time, because fuel pressure is held constant.

quiz.q: Why does mono-point give poorer cylinder-to-cylinder fuel distribution than multi-point?
quiz.a: Mono-point delivers fuel at one central point, so manifold geometry and wall wetting affect how much fuel reaches each cylinder. Multi-point injects at each port, close to the valve.

quiz.q: An injector flows 180 cm³/min. It opens for 8 ms. Find fuel per injection in mm³.
quiz.a: 180 cm³/min = 3 cm³/s. Time = 0.008 s. Volume = 3 × 0.008 = 0.024 cm³ = 24 mm³.

quiz.q: A car with GDI shows intake valve carbon deposits. Explain why this is more likely than in port injection.
quiz.a: In GDI, fuel does not wash the intake port or valve, so crankcase vapours and deposits bake onto the valve; port injection sprays fuel on the valve and keeps it cleaner.

quiz.q: Name the two GDI charge modes.
What is the difference between open loop and closed loop?
quiz.a: Open loop uses stored tables and ignores the oxygen sensor. Closed loop uses the oxygen sensor to trim the pulse width toward stoichiometric.

quiz.q: A four-cylinder engine uses sequential injection. How many injector pulses occur per four-stroke cycle?
quiz.a: Four, one per cylinder per cycle.

beyond: Not for the exam. Production GDI systems now run up to about 350 bar and use gasoline particulate filters to control the fine particles that direct injection creates. Some engines use dual injection: port injectors for low load and direct injectors for high load, which keeps intake valves clean. Wideband oxygen sensors give a continuous lambda reading instead of a switch, so the ECU can run lean stratified mixtures safely. Model-based air charge estimation replaces some sensors with software models. Search for gasoline particulate filter, dual injection and wideband lambda sensor.
